lines: Ever wondered why the bottom of ships is red?
Anything that sits in the ocean gets covered in life.
And a dirty hull drags through the water,
which burns a lot more fuel.
Hundreds of years ago, sailors found a trick.
They covered wooden hulls in copper sheets.
Copper is toxic to those critters, so they stay off.
Later, ships switched to paint with copper in it.
And that copper paint was usually red.
Today, it can be almost any color.
But red stuck around. Mostly out of tradition.
